elements.element: No non-compete restriction imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: 12.4 "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor"; 12.3 "Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service"
12.3 "or conducting business in any field or territory"; 12.4 permission extends "in any territory"

elements.element: Restriction limited to a single named competing product
elements.evidence: 12.4 refers to "any product or service that competes with Vendor" — no named product; and no restriction remains at all

elements.element: Restriction operative during the term only
elements.evidence: "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter" retained, though now framed as a permission

elements.element: Carve-out for internal development and acquisitions
elements.evidence: No carve-out language inserted; 12.4 contains no exceptions clause

reasons: The locked preferred level is achieved: the single operator change from "shall not" to "may" removes the only non-compete/field-of-use restriction on Customer, and § 12.3's affirmative no-exclusivity/no-non-compete acknowledgement remains intact.

Minimality is satisfied — one short phrase was replaced rather than rewriting or deleting the paragraph, and no new exceptions, obligations or fallback-only mechanics (named product, 12-month cap, carve-outs) were imported.

Intent is preserved: the residual lead-in "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter" now merely bounds a permission and creates no undefined term or dangling obligation, and the contradiction with § 12.3 is resolved.

Fallback elements are unmet, but that is immaterial because preferred and fallback are separate bargains and the preferred position is fully achieved; the fallback is offered only in the non-operative comment.
